- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, suggesting overshoot after initial spikes.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter half of the 30-day window, particularly after mid-range values.
- Strong mean reversion bias: forecasts drift downward after initial peaks, but true values often remain higher or stabilize at mid-range.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in late periods; true values often dip below forecasted lows.
- Forecast horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then overly pessimistic in the last 10 days.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price drops — fails to adjust forecast downward quickly after sharp declines.
- Overshoot correction: if forecast exceeds true value by >5% in early days, reduce by 2–3% for next period.
- Mean reversion trigger: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, apply downward adjustment of 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs: if last 5 days are rising, don’t assume continuation; cap forecast at 10% below recent peak.
